claim: A video captures an experiment in which immersing an egg in soda for 24 hours dissolved its shell and turned the egg into a rubbery, squeezable substance.
label: false
explain: In May 2019, a video showing the bizarre reaction that supposedly takes place when an egg is immersed for 24 hours in soft drinks such as Coca-Cola and Pepsi went viral on Facebook. The original video, which was posted to TikTok by @blogerwojciech, can be seen below:This video supposedly shows an eggshell being dissolved in Coca-Cola and Pepsi, leaving behind a rubbery, squeezable sac. Blogerwojciech didn’t provide much of an explanation for how this reaction allegedly occurred, writing only that Cola + Pepsi + 🥚+ 24godziny 😵 Zaskoczeni (Cola + Pepsi + 🥚+ 24 hours = surprised).This video, however, does not showcase some sort of bizarre chemical reaction, but rather how some clever edits and an egg toy can entertain millions of viewers on social media.One immediate red flag is that the egg in this video is hidden from view when the filmmaker places a mug over the soda-filled cup, and then again when it’s retrieved from behind a sign reading “24 H.” In other words, the viewer has no idea how much time has really elapsed and never actually sees the eggshell dissolving.Hiding the egg in this manner (as well as cutting down an alleged 24-hour time span to just a few seconds) would make it easy for the filmmaker to switch out the real egg with a prop — perhaps with some sort of squishy, egg-stress ball toy, such as this product available via Amazon:We reached out to @blogerwojciech and he confirmed via email that he used a fake egg in the viral video. @blogerwojciecj also directed us to another one of his TikTok videos in which he revealed how the video was made:While this video certainly employs some trickery, it is reminiscent of a classic,  “eggsperiment”: When an egg is soaked in a subtance such as vinegar for multiple hours, the shell will dissolve and leave behind a “naked egg” that you can (kind of) bounce on a table:While this naked egg will “bounce,” the contents inside the membrane don’t harden the way they supposedly do in the viral TikTok video. If you squeeze the naked egg too hard, the membrane will crack, and its contents will spill out.Here’s a video of the egg-in-vinegar experiment. Finally , remove the egg from the fridge to see if the shell be dissolve , and put it back for one more day if it be n't . If you want to dissolve an eggshell , start by place an egg in a glass and add enough vinegar or cola to cover it . For the best result , cover the glass with some plastic wrap or foil , then place it on a shelf in your refrigerator for 24 hour . If you have a hard time get your child to brush his teeth , it might be time to try the egg and soda experiment to explore the concept of dental health . The first be that , a report in the Journal of Zhejiang University , the acid contain in soda , as well a the carbonation , have enormous potential to erode tooth enamel.﻿﻿ In fact , one study report that the acid and sugar in soda can cause severe dental caries—tooth decay—and erode tooth enamel.﻿﻿ The study find that drink soda regularly over the course of seven year can severely decay the incisor and the canine and also cause some damage to the premolar and the molar . Unfortunately , some of our eating and drinking habit make it difficult for the enamel to protect our teeth from damage , and the egg and soda experiment demonstrate how our dietary choice can impact our body . In theory , a hard-boiled egg ’ s shell work similarly to the enamel on a child ’ s tooth . As a variation , you might also want to boil a few extra egg and add cup with clear soda , orange juice , and coffee for comparison . Show him a hard-boiled egg and ask him how it remind him of his teeth ( a hard but thin outer shell and a soft inside ) . You might also consider different type of soda and if dark soda , like cola , might have different effect on teeth than clear soda , like lemon-lime soda .
